territorial_scope.description: Applies to purchases by New York State and its governmental units, and to discriminatory practices under New York State Executive Law.

evidence.provision: Section 1 (State Finance Law §165, subd. 9, para. b)
evidence.quote: When purchasing a product or service that is or contains an algorithmic decision system to be used by the state, a state unit shall purchase a product or service that adheres to responsible artificial intelligence standards

summary.short: Amends New York State Finance Law §165 to require state units purchasing algorithmic decision systems to buy products that adhere to responsible AI standards (harm avoidance, transparency, fairness, impact evaluation). Amends Executive Law §292 so that unlawful discriminatory practices include those performed through an algorithmic decision system. Takes effect January 1 after enactment.
summary.long: The bill adds subdivision 9 to State Finance Law §165. It defines an algorithmic decision system as a computational process that makes or facilitates decisions impacting individuals, and defines a state unit as the state, its agencies, political subdivisions and public benefit corporations. When a state unit purchases a product or service that is or contains such a system for state use, it must buy one that adheres to responsible AI standards: minimizing risks of physical or mental injury, unjustified deletion or disclosure of information, and unwarranted damage; full disclosure to the state unit of the system's capabilities, limitations and potential problems; fairness, including eliminating discrimination and providing a feedback avenue to redress harms; and a comprehensive evaluation of impact and risks. The commissioner of taxation and finance must adopt regulations to carry out the subdivision. The bill also amends Executive Law §292(4) so that the term unlawful discriminatory practice includes an act prohibited under the listed provisions that is performed through an algorithmic decision system. The act takes effect on the first of January next succeeding its enactment. The bill is at the introduced stage and was referred to the Committee on Governmental Operations.

relations.note: Adds a new subdivision 9 (algorithmic decision system purchase rules) to section 165.

notes: Bill introduced 2023-03-07 and referred to the Committee on Governmental Operations; registry status pending. Section 3 sets the effective date as the first of January next succeeding enactment. The Executive Law amendment cross-references the definition in State Finance Law section 165 subdivision 9 that Section 1 adds, so the two amendments depend on each other. Section 2 cites an earlier amendment by chapter 57 of the laws of 2018 (subpart F of part KK), which this bill does not itself change. Target instrument IDs are empty because the amended laws are not in the registry.
